_readme: THE HOST'S OWN DEFAULT. No agent uses this file.
Each of the four agents brings its own policy, one file per agent in profiles\,
and that is what its tool calls compile. Editing this file does not change what
any agent on screen can do. If that is what you came here for, open the Policy
tab and pick an agent, or edit profiles\<agent>.json directly.
What still reads this file is the machinery that belongs to no single agent:
the Run tab's dry run, the network dialect negotiation at startup, and verify.py.
Those make a claim about this machine rather than about an agent, and they must
not borrow one agent's boundary to make it. That is the only reason this file
The fields are identical to a profile's, so this is also the worked example of
Every field below maps to a real field in the MXC wire schema. See COMPILED.md,
or hit the 'Show the JSON that MXC actually receives' button in the Policy tab.
name: host-default
description: The host's own default, used by the dry run, the startup dialect check and verify.py. No agent runs under it. The grants below are deliberately middling: wide enough that a dialect probe and a verify run can actually start a sandbox, and attached to nobody, so they hand nothing to anything.

paths._note: Grant the least you can. ${windir}\System32 is what cmd.exe, powershell.exe and curl.exe themselves live in - take it away and the sandbox cannot even start the tool. Resist adding ${project} or ${home} here: a broad grant does not announce itself, it just quietly makes every refusal you were counting on stop happening.

network._note: outbound: 'deny' | 'allow'. Per-host rules are NOT supported on Windows by this binary - it is all or nothing. The model itself runs on the host and never crosses this boundary.

ui._note: What the sandboxed process may do to your desktop.

advanced._note: leastPrivilege is not representable at the BaseContainer tier and will push the run down to AppContainer. learningMode logs denied access to diagnostics without allowing it. captureDenials writes a JSON receipt of everything that was refused - it needs host support and may be unavailable; CastleKeep will tell you rather than pretend.

tools._note: Turn individual tools off entirely. This is a HOST-side gate - it stops the tool before it ever reaches a sandbox. Leave these on to watch MXC do the refusing instead; that is the honest demo.
